trk.title: Tracking
trk.sub: What the shop's server tells the ad platforms: a product seen, put in the bag, the checkout opened, an order placed, confirmed and delivered. Each platform counts an event once.
trk.off: Tracking is off. Nothing is recorded or sent. Switch it on in the card at the bottom.
trk.noPlatform: Tracking is on but no platform is ticked: events are recorded here and sent nowhere. Tick the platforms in the card at the bottom.

mode.MOCK: Practice copy — nothing leaves the shop

trk.waitingLine: {n} events wait for a platform (new ones, or failed ones with tries left). They are sent with the next event, or now:
trk.testLine: Sends one sample event (your newest product) to every platform in its test mode. On a practice copy nothing leaves the shop; on a live one it shows under the platform's Test events and is never counted.
trk.outcome: {platform}: {sent} sent, {mock} to the practice copy, {failed} failed
trk.noManage: You can see this page; changing it needs the "Switch server-side tracking on or off" permission.

card.d: Off as it ships. Keys are typed on Keys & connections, never here.
card.on: Send events to the ad platforms from the server
card.onHelp: Off: nothing is recorded or sent.
card.matchHelp: The platforms match an event to a person by a one-way code (hash) of the phone and e-mail. The number itself never leaves the shop. Off: only the shop's own random visitor code goes.
card.attemptsHelp: After this many failed tries an event is left as failed.
card.readOnly: You can see these settings; changing them needs the manage permission.

attr.d: On as it ships. Keeps the campaign tags (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign) and the ad click id of a visit on the order it leads to, so Profit & loss by channel and the order export can count ad sales.
attr.on: Keep where an order came from
attr.onHelp: Off: a visit from an ad or campaign link is not remembered and orders keep no source.
attr.daysHelp: An order placed within this many days of the ad visit keeps its tags (1 to 90).
attr.touchHelp: The latest tagged visit wins, or the first one stays until its days are over.

err.STALE: Someone changed this meanwhile; the page was read again. Try once more.
err.INVALID_INPUT: Something in it is not right. Check the fields.
err.forbidden: You do not have permission for this.
err.unauthorized: Your sign-in ran out. Sign in again.
err.other: It did not work. Try again.

trk.dpTrackingOff: Delivered sales are switched on, but tracking is off: no order step is recorded until tracking is on (the card at the bottom).
trk.dpMeansDelivered: The platforms count a purchase at the delivery: a parcel delivered goes under their purchase name, and an order placed goes as "Order placed".

dp.d: For a cash-on-delivery shop the sale is the parcel the customer accepted. While this and tracking are on, each order's confirmation and its delivery are sent from the order's own timeline, with the value of the pieces kept. Off as it ships. No money moves and no ad budget changes.
dp.onHelp: Off: no order step is recorded, and a purchase stays the order placed.
dp.means: A purchase on the ad platforms means
dp.meansHelp: The ads learn from what you call a purchase. "Parcel delivered" teaches them who accepts parcels, not who orders and refuses. Changing it starts the platforms' learning again, so choose once.
dp.lookbackHelp: Steps older than this are not sent. The platforms take events up to 7 days (168 hours) old.
dp.everyHelp: "Send waiting now" reads it at once too.

trk.stepsRead: {n} new order steps read from the order timeline.
trk.feedRidesOff: The deep conversion feed is switched on, but it rides on tracking and on delivered sales: nothing of it is recorded until both are on (the cards at the bottom).
trk.feedGenerous: On {platforms} a purchase is now the qualified sale: delivered, or with the courier untouched for your hours; an order placed goes as "Order placed" and a delivery as "Parcel delivered" there.

feed.d: The ad platforms also learn the courier's side of each order (handed to the courier, came back) and, on the platforms you tick as generous, the qualified sale: delivered, or with the courier untouched for your hours — held back only when cancelled or marked bad. Every order event also carries the courier outcome and the visitor's intent; never a name, address, phone or e-mail. Rides on tracking and on delivered sales (their sources, look-back and clock). Off as it ships. No money moves and no ad budget changes.
feed.onHelp: Off: no courier step and no qualified sale is recorded, and order events go without the outcome and intent.
feed.generous: Platforms where a purchase is the qualified sale
feed.hold: Hours with the courier before it counts
feed.holdHelp: An order handed to the courier counts as a qualified sale after this many hours, if nobody cancelled it or marked it bad meanwhile. 0 = at once. A delivery always counts at once.
feed.flags: Order flags that mark an order bad (never a qualified sale)
feed.blocked: A number on the blocklist marks the order bad
feed.blockedHelp: An order from a number on the blocklist (or marked by it) is never sent as a qualified sale.
feed.enrich_courier: The courier outcome (what happened, the courier, the days, the payment kind)
feed.enrich_intent: The visitor's intent (channel, campaign, ad click, returning customer, products seen, bag adds, checkouts)
feed.days: Days of visits counted for the intent
feed.daysHelp: The products seen, bag adds and checkouts of the same visitor or customer in these days before the order.
feed.withdraw: A returned parcel takes the purchase back
feed.withdrawHelp: Off: a parcel that came back goes as its own “returned” event everywhere. On: where the platform can take a purchase back (Google Analytics’ refund, the same order number), a returned parcel withdraws the purchase it already counted; Meta and TikTok cannot, so there it stays the returned event. Only what the ad platforms are told changes; no money moves.
feed.share: Share the event ids with a browser pixel
feed.shareHelp: Off: nothing is added to the thank-you page. On: the thank-you page carries one hidden data block (id “extas-event-ids”, no code) listing, for each ticked platform, every event the shop's server will send for that order with its name and id. A pixel you add through a tag manager can fire its event under the same id, so the platform counts the two once. Only the order number and event names; never a name, phone, e-mail or amount.
